claim: One bounded sanitized cohort of ten multi-turn workflow-decision scenarios was run once each, serially, in the foreground against one disclosed Host model, all ten under one fixture. Every scenario reached completed and was graded criterion by criterion from the concrete transcript decisions, with every required criterion linked to the recorded observation that substantiates it. Eight scenarios met every required criterion. Two genuinely failed and are disclosed: partial-publication-receipt-recovery did not name the required first-readback contents, and bounded-discovery-and-partial-edit-recovery reverted a partially applied patch instead of completing only the unfinished file. Both failures are recorded as failed, not as cosmetic deviations. The workflow contract is correct on both behaviors; the under-test model deviates.
claim_limits: This is one cohort of ten scenarios on one disclosed model; it does not prove universal Host or provider correctness.
Each scenario received exactly one attempt in this run; no scenario was retried in place and no criterion was rewritten to fit an answer.

Two of the ten scenarios are recorded as failed: the cohort reports 8 passed and 2 failed, and each failed scenario's unmet criterion and observed deviation are disclosed here and in the report. A failure cannot be disclosed as a pass, a cosmetic deviation, or hidden totals.

Every required criterion of every scenario is linked to the specific recorded transcript decision that substantiates it, so a pass cannot stand while the observation that would support one of its criteria was never recorded.
The failure is a bounded observation of one model on one scenario; it is not evidence that the workflow contract is wrong, and this cohort claims no workflow contract change.
Cost and runtime advisory telemetry are unavailable from this Host and are recorded as unknown, not zero.
Scenarios performed no real commit, GitHub write or Enrollment.
This report does not fix the external H1 Host-producer issue.
Two earlier generations of this cohort were discarded and are not evidence; see cohort_provenance.supersedes.

runner.model_selection_evidence: `pi --list-models` lists `gemini-3.6-flash` under provider `antigravity`; a direct foreground probe returned the expected text before the cohort. Each scenario dispatch passed the explicit `model: antigravity/gemini-3.6-flash` override.

source_bindings.note: Bindings are content hashes (sha256) of the tracked artifacts at delivery, not a Git HEAD pointer, because the synthetic reviewed revision differs from the execution workspace. Only the offline verifier is bound as runner_source and it is re-hashed from disk. No execution-time runner revision is declared, because live dispatch is Parent-mediated through the foreground Agent tool and no script executes during a scenario; claiming such a revision would assert bytes no offline check could tie to the cohort.

reasons: It recorded attempts_total=10 and one attempt per scenario while the execution log shows twelve dispatches, because the integration and zero-question scenarios were each dispatched twice.
The zero-question scenario's required turn was rewritten after the first answer was read, so the graded criterion was changed to fit the answer.
It classified the bulk-approval and partial-edit answers as passed although a required criterion of each was unmet, by treating partial credit as a pass.

It was a mixed generation: eight scenarios came from a run under the pre-correction fixture, and only the outbound-channel and bounded-discovery scenarios were re-run after the fixture was corrected, so it would have reported a single coherent cohort while actually mixing two fixture revisions.

Its source bindings declared an execution-time runner digest that no offline check could tie to any reviewable bytes; live dispatch is Parent-mediated, so the corrected contract rejects an execution-time runner claim outright rather than policing it.

fixture_corrections: unlocked-branches-after-bulk-approval: the two dependent branches now carry no recommendation, so the batch approval genuinely cannot decide them and the scenario measures re-asking on the newly unblocked frontier.
clear-zero-question-request: the turn no longer supplies the expected single branch as a hint; it asks for the sourced branch generally, so the answer is not graded against leaked prompt text.

new-outbound-channel-delta: the prompt now supplies all four sources (article, mock, read-only database, colleague's model-quality note) and the turn asks the answer to classify its evidence, so the four-class criterion is elicitable from the prompt rather than assumed.

bounded-discovery-and-partial-edit-recovery: the partial patch belongs to the task's own implementation step, the probe's listing is genuinely truncated, and the checklist now additionally covers reading the remaining bounded pages instead of re-running a broad search.

provenance.collection: foreground Agent tool results read by the Parent; each scenario's text was graded criterion by criterion against the cohort's successChecklist
provenance.grading: every required criterion of every scenario was linked to the recorded transcript decision that substantiates it and graded against that observation; a scenario passes only when all of its criteria are met and every assessment agrees with the recorded outcome
provenance.retention: sanitized decisions only; no raw transcript, secret or credential is stored
provenance.dispatch: parent-mediated foreground Agent dispatch: the Parent read each foreground Agent tool result directly and graded every criterion itself; no child self-report was trusted and no native confirmation was impersonated.
